about.profile.approach: That is where discovery and technical scoping do the real work: naming the users, the business rules, the integration boundaries and the success criteria, then getting to a prototype fast enough that the conversation can continue against something real. I care about what the system actually does, not only whether the interface looks convincing.

ajoop.hub.title: The portfolio, in conversation.
ajoop.hub.lead: AJOOP is the public assistant built into this site. Ask it about Kaan's projects, experience, skills and how to reach him; it answers from the published portfolio and shows the evidence it used.
ajoop.hub.noscript: AJOOP needs JavaScript to hold a conversation. Everything it draws on is published on these pages.
ajoop.hub.loading: The conversation opens here once this page's scripts are running.
ajoop.hub.scope.heading: Answers from
ajoop.hub.bounds.private: No access to private accounts or files
ajoop.hub.path.heading: This turn
ajoop.hub.evidence.heading: Evidence in this answer
ajoop.hub.evidence.empty: When an answer cites portfolio records, they are listed here.
ajoop.hub.evidence.general: A general answer: no portfolio records were used.
ajoop.hub.evidence.assistFailed: AI assistance was unavailable for this answer; it comes from the deterministic portfolio answers.
ajoop.hub.evidence.failed: No answer could be prepared for this turn.
ajoop.case.hero.lead: A local-first portfolio assistant that answers from Kaan's published portfolio knowledge, shows the evidence behind each answer, and keeps working when its AI model is switched off.
ajoop.case.problem.title: A portfolio chatbot that guesses is worse than no chatbot.
ajoop.case.problem.body: A recruiter asking a portfolio assistant about a project needs the same facts the case study states. A generic chatbot can sound fluent while mixing up projects, inventing a stack, or answering about a different person with the same name.
ajoop.case.problem.detail: AJOOP started from the opposite requirement: every portfolio claim has to come from the canonical portfolio data, and an answer has to exist even when no model is running.
ajoop.case.goal.title: Natural, grounded and coherent.
ajoop.case.goal.natural: Answers read like conversation, not like a lookup table
ajoop.case.goal.grounded: Every portfolio claim traces to published portfolio data
ajoop.case.goal.coherent: A follow-up question keeps its subject
ajoop.case.goal.honest: The assistant says what it does not know
ajoop.case.arch.title: One public path from question to grounded answer.
ajoop.case.arch.body: The browser never holds a model or a secret. It plans a complete deterministic answer first, offers the turn to a local model through a public bridge, and commits exactly one answer.
ajoop.case.arch.rest: Select a part of the path to see what it does.
ajoop.case.node.visitor.body: Types a question or picks a prompt, in any of the site's five languages.
ajoop.case.node.ui.body: The site launcher and the AJOOP Hub: two presentations of one conversation.
ajoop.case.node.state.body: A bounded window of recent turns, kept for this tab only, so a follow-up keeps its subject.
ajoop.case.node.planner.body: Routes the question and prepares a complete answer from canonical portfolio data. It always runs.
ajoop.case.node.bridge.body: Optional. Retrieves the portfolio records a question is about and lets a local model phrase the answer. When it is off, slow or wrong, the planned answer is used.
ajoop.case.node.evidence.body: The canonical portfolio data: projects, experience, skills and certificates. The only source of portfolio facts.
ajoop.case.node.answer.body: One answer per turn, with its evidence cards and a line saying where it came from.
ajoop.case.node.owner.body: Private, read-only connectors that only Kaan uses with his own accounts. They are a separate track and cannot be reached from public AJOOP.
ajoop.case.ground.title: The model may phrase an answer. It may not supply the facts.
ajoop.case.ground.canonical.title: Canonical data first
ajoop.case.ground.canonical.body: Portfolio facts live once, in the portfolio's own data files. The assistant, Recruiter Mode and the project pages read the same records.
ajoop.case.ground.retrieval.title: Retrieval, then generation
ajoop.case.ground.retrieval.body: For a portfolio question the bridge retrieves the records the question is about, and the model answers from those. A general question is answered as ordinary conversation, with no portfolio records attached.
ajoop.case.ground.cards.title: Evidence on the answer
ajoop.case.ground.cards.body: A portfolio answer carries its evidence cards, links and a provenance line. A general answer is prose and nothing else.
ajoop.case.ground.validated.title: Validated replies
ajoop.case.ground.validated.body: Every reply from the bridge is treated as untrusted and checked before it is shown. A reply that fails the check is discarded for the planned answer.
ajoop.case.flow.title: A follow-up should not have to repeat its subject.
ajoop.case.flow.step3: Turn offered to the local model
ajoop.case.flow.memory.title: Bounded memory
ajoop.case.flow.memory.body: Only a short window of recent turns travels with a question: enough for "and its stack?" to know which project is meant.
ajoop.case.flow.shared.title: Launcher and Hub, one conversation
ajoop.case.flow.shared.body: The launcher and the Hub share one conversation. A bounded copy is kept in this tab's session storage for up to 15 minutes so it survives a page change; it is cleared by Start over, by a language change and when the tab session ends.
ajoop.case.safe.title: Built to fail closed.
ajoop.case.safe.boundary.title: Public and private are separate
ajoop.case.safe.boundary.body: Public AJOOP reads published portfolio content only. Owner-only tools are a separate track; no visitor question can reach them.
ajoop.case.safe.live.title: No invented live data
ajoop.case.safe.live.body: AJOOP has no web access. Asked for weather, prices or news, it says so instead of guessing.
ajoop.case.safe.restricted.title: Restricted material is absent
ajoop.case.safe.restricted.body: Anything not marked public is removed before the knowledge base is built, so it cannot be retrieved.
ajoop.case.safe.fallback.title: The model is never a dependency
ajoop.case.safe.fallback.body: If the bridge is off, busy, slow or returns something malformed, the visitor still gets the deterministic answer.
ajoop.case.safe.internal.title: Infrastructure stays internal
ajoop.case.safe.internal.body: The public assistant is instructed never to reveal private infrastructure details, and the browser's public configuration holds no token or secret.
ajoop.case.evo.title: From keyword replies to a retrieval-backed assistant.
ajoop.case.evo.step2: A router with entities, context and evidence cards
ajoop.case.evo.step3: A local model that restates grounded answers
ajoop.case.evo.step4: Retrieval-first turns with a deterministic fallback
ajoop.case.evo.body: The local, free engine remains the default, and the deterministic assistant remains the product underneath it.
ajoop.case.decide.title: Three rules the system is built around.
ajoop.case.decide.once.title: Commit once per turn
ajoop.case.decide.once.body: One container, one answer. The visitor never watches one answer being replaced by another.
ajoop.case.decide.secrets.title: Keep the browser free of secrets
ajoop.case.decide.secrets.body: The public configuration is an endpoint and two time limits. Retrieval, scope selection and generation stay behind the bridge.
ajoop.case.decide.boring.title: Let failure be boring
ajoop.case.decide.boring.body: Every failure path ends in an answer the visitor can use, and says so in one short line.
ajoop.case.live.title: Ask it yourself.
ajoop.case.live.body: The assistant described here is the one running on this site.
privacy.storage.browser: Your theme and language choices are saved in your browser's local storage. AJOOP and Recruiter Mode keep minimal state for the current visit in session storage. AJOOP does not permanently retain your messages. To keep the launcher and AJOOP Hub in sync, a bounded copy of the current conversation may be stored temporarily in this browser tab’s session storage for up to 15 minutes. It is cleared when you start over, change language, or end the tab session.

mergeRush.play.lead: A compact factory-floor puzzle where every merge matters because an order clock is running. Place parts, merge twins into the next tier and deliver what each order asks for before the four-minute run ends.
mergeRush.play.steps.heading: How a run goes
mergeRush.play.steps.1.title: Place and merge
mergeRush.play.steps.1.body: Drag the next part onto the grid. Two identical parts merge into the next tier, from Bolt up to Factory Core.
mergeRush.play.steps.2.title: Deliver the order
mergeRush.play.steps.2.body: One timed order is always active. Drag the product it asks for to the Delivery Bay; back-to-back deliveries build a combo up to x4.
mergeRush.play.steps.3.title: Restore the factory
mergeRush.play.steps.3.body: Score unlocks more of the 5×5 floor across five levels. At Level 5 the final order is the Factory Core; delivering it wins the run and opens Endless Mode.
mergeRush.play.noscript: Merge Rush needs JavaScript to run. The case study explains how it was built.
mergeRush.play.error.title: Merge Rush could not load
mergeRush.play.error.body: Part of the game did not arrive. Check your connection and try again, or read how it was built instead.
mergeRush.case.statusNote: Playable V1 — playable on this site
mergeRush.case.lead: A factory-floor merge puzzle where a running order clock makes every merge matter: place parts on a 5×5 grid, merge twins up a six-tier ladder and deliver what each timed order asks for.
mergeRush.case.hosts: This portfolio · browser tab · YouTube Playables adapter
mergeRush.case.privateNote: The game is developed in its own private repository; this site ships its production build.
mergeRush.case.posterAlt: Merge Rush mid-run: the 5×5 board, the active order, the Delivery Bay and the next queue
mergeRush.case.problem.title: Make a merge matter beyond matching two identical parts.
mergeRush.case.problem.p1: A merge board without a goal is a tidy-up exercise. Merge Rush gives every merge a customer: one timed order is always active, and only the product it asks for can be delivered.
mergeRush.case.problem.p2: Score from deliveries is what opens more of the floor, so short-term order pressure and long-term board space are one loop rather than two systems.
mergeRush.case.goal.body: A new player should understand place → merge → deliver within the first order. Combo, staged unlocks, the final Factory Core order and Endless damage and repair arrive after that, one at a time.
mergeRush.case.loop.score: Score with a combo of up to x4
mergeRush.case.loop.unlock: Unlock more of the 5×5 floor across five levels
mergeRush.case.loop.core: Build and deliver the final Factory Core
mergeRush.case.eng.title: The rules are a pure state machine; the scene only draws it.
mergeRush.case.eng.state.title: Pure GameState
mergeRush.case.eng.state.body: Board, queue, orders, combo, levels, win, loss and Endless damage live in one class with no Phaser and no DOM. The same class runs under the tests, the balance simulation and the browser.
mergeRush.case.eng.weights.title: Weighted generation
mergeRush.case.eng.weights.body: The next queue and the order tier are drawn from per-level weight tables, so each level changes what arrives and what is asked for without special cases in code.
mergeRush.case.eng.deadlock.body: A full board is only a loss when no merge, no delivery and no direct merge from the queue is left. The check runs after every action and the result screen states the reason.
mergeRush.case.prog.title: The factory floor is the progress bar.
mergeRush.case.prog.1.title: Level 1 · 9 cells
mergeRush.case.prog.1.body: The central 3×3 and four Bolts. Orders ask for Gears only.
mergeRush.case.prog.2.title: Level 2 · 13 cells
mergeRush.case.prog.2.body: At 400 points. Motors join the orders and the queue.
mergeRush.case.prog.3.title: Level 3 · 17 cells
mergeRush.case.prog.3.body: At 1,000 points. Machines start to be ordered.
mergeRush.case.prog.4.title: Level 4 · 21 cells
mergeRush.case.prog.4.body: At 2,000 points. Robot orders appear; Gears are no longer ordered.
mergeRush.case.prog.5.title: Level 5 · 25 cells
mergeRush.case.prog.5.body: At 3,500 points. The whole floor is open and the only order left is the Factory Core.
mergeRush.case.arch.title: One build, three hosts: a browser tab, this portfolio and YouTube Playables.
mergeRush.case.arch.embed.title: Embed contract
mergeRush.case.arch.embed.body: The game exports one mount function. The portfolio passes the locale and receives ready, exit, win and game-over events; leaving the page destroys the canvas, its audio and its listeners.
mergeRush.case.arch.lifecycle.body: A hidden tab or a host pause freezes both timers and the audio. The run waits on its pause screen and never resumes by itself.
mergeRush.case.arch.assets.title: Asset pipeline
mergeRush.case.arch.assets.body: Art masters stay in the source repository. The shipped set is WebP and Ogg with an MP3 fallback, drawn at device resolution up to 2×, and the engine is requested only when Play is pressed.
mergeRush.case.qa.title: Rules are tested as rules; input is tested as input.
mergeRush.case.qa.body: 82 automated tests cover the rules, with negative controls: different tiers never merge, a delivery pays once, a paused or hidden run does not drain, and victory comes only from the final Core. A browser pass then plays whole runs with real pointer and touch drags.
mergeRush.case.status.title: What is playable now, and what is still open.
mergeRush.case.status.done: Factory Run with five levels and the final Core order, Endless Mode with damage and repair, onboarding, pause, results, a saved best score and audio settings, touch and pointer play, and five locales.
mergeRush.case.status.open: Verification on real devices beyond emulation, pacing for practised players (a practised run finishes well inside the four minutes) and a release on a game platform.
mergeRush.case.cta.title: Play a run, then see the rest of the game work.
mergeRush.card.games: Timed orders, a six-tier merge ladder, level-by-level floor unlocks, an Endless mode with damage and repair, and a host-aware build.
mergeRush.card.works: Stateful product engineering through timed orders, a pure rules engine, level-based unlocks, responsive layouts, automated tests and a host-aware build.

career.case.lead: A drop-and-merge physics game in which the ladder is a career: two of the same object merge into the next, from Book to Job Offer, in a chamber that must not overflow.
career.case.coverAlt: Career Adventure in play: the board, the career path and the next piece
career.case.proof.runs: Strategy runs checked step by step
career.case.concept.title: A career, told as a drop-and-merge game.
career.case.concept.p1: The thirteen rungs are, in order: Book, Keyboard, Mouse, Monitor, HTML / CSS, JavaScript, Python, C# / .NET, Database, AI Flow, Portfolio, Interview, Job Offer. Their order did not change in the rewrite.
career.case.concept.p2: The first version was a small in-page toy. Its physics advanced once per frame, its game-over rule could not be met in play, and dropping in a single position won.
career.case.goal.title: The same game, made real.
career.case.goal.body: Keep the loop and the ladder; replace everything under and around them: the simulation, the difficulty, the endings, the shell and the checks.
career.case.engine.title: A deterministic simulation under a clock.
career.case.engine.step.title: Fixed timestep
career.case.engine.step.body: The simulation advances in whole steps of 1/120 s, at most twelve per frame, so the game is the same at 30 Hz and at 240 Hz.
career.case.engine.rest.title: Stacks that rest
career.case.engine.rest.body: Contacts are solved from the floor up with impulses carried from step to step, so a pile rests instead of sinking into itself.
career.case.engine.pure.title: Rules without a page
career.case.engine.pure.body: The simulation is a plain object that touches no DOM and reads no clock. The file the page ships also runs in Node, where the strategy runs are played.
career.case.engine.replay.title: Deterministic replay
career.case.engine.replay.body: The same seed and the same drops give the same run. A recorded winning run is replayed through the page's own clock and compared with the run outside the browser.
career.case.difficulty.title: Winning has to come from planning, not from a trick.
career.case.difficulty.body: Each naive strategy was played 200 times on the shipped simulation, and none reached the Job Offer. A simple planner that looks one drop ahead reached it in 5 of 16 runs, and in 10 of 16 when it also used both tools. Difficulty comes from the chamber's geometry and the spawn pool; nothing in the simulation watches how the player is doing.
career.case.difficulty.tools: Looks ahead and uses both tools
career.case.difficulty.note: The last two are small samples of a simple planner, not a model of a person.
career.case.rules.title: A game over that can happen, and an ending that is earned.
career.case.rules.over.title: Game over
career.case.rules.over.body: A landed object that stays above the line for 2.2 seconds ends the run. The timer runs down twice as fast as it runs up, so a bounce does not.
career.case.rules.score.title: Scoring
career.case.rules.score.body: Creating rung n pays 5·n·(n+1). A merge within 0.8 s of the last continues a chain worth up to ×2, and the Job Offer adds 5,000.
career.case.rules.tools.title: Two tools
career.case.rules.tools.body: Re-scope swaps the object in hand with the next one; Debug removes the smallest object. Five milestones on the ladder refill one of each.
career.case.rules.win.title: Victory
career.case.rules.win.body: The last merge is the Job Offer. Neither ending restarts the game by itself; both show the run and offer what to do next.
career.case.shell.title: A full-viewport game with its own menu, HUD and results.
career.case.shell.body: Play enters a full-viewport mode: the site's header, footer and floating controls step out, and one history entry is added so that Back returns to the page. A touch drops on lifting the finger, a mouse on click, the keyboard on Space or Enter. Sound is synthesised in the browser; the game loads no image, font or audio file.
career.case.status.title: What is done, and what is still open.
career.case.status.done: Menu, a run with its HUD, pause, victory and game over; chains, milestones, two tools and three rooms; a saved profile; five languages; a reduced-effects mode and keyboard play.
career.case.status.open: Touch, safe areas, vibration and frame pacing were checked in emulation only. Landscape phones get a reduced layout, and the planner's win rate is a small sample.
career.case.cta.title: Drop a Book and see how far the ladder goes.
portfolio.case.statusNote: In production — you are reading it
portfolio.case.lead: A portfolio built as a system: one registry of projects, statically prerendered React in five languages, a public assistant and four games, each loaded only where it is used.
portfolio.case.proof.servers: Servers needed to serve a page
portfolio.case.evolution.title: From hand-written pages to one prerendered system.
portfolio.case.evolution.p1: The site began as static HTML pages with a shared stylesheet and script. Every project lived in several places at once: a card, a detail page and a data object.
portfolio.case.evolution.p2: V4, the Connected Systems version, keeps the static deployment and replaces the hand-maintained copies: pages are rendered from canonical data at build time and hydrated in the browser.
portfolio.case.why.title: Components without a server.
portfolio.case.why.body: React gives the pages one component model and real state for the catalog, the assistant and Recruiter Mode. Prerendering keeps what static hosting gives: every route is an HTML file that works before any script runs.
portfolio.case.arch.title: One registry, many surfaces.
portfolio.case.arch.registry.title: Canonical registry
portfolio.case.arch.registry.body: Projects, profile, build log and the coverage catalog are JSON files. Works, Games, project pages, case studies and the assistant's public evidence are built from them.
portfolio.case.arch.prerender.title: Prerender and hydration
portfolio.case.arch.prerender.body: A build script renders every route in every language to static HTML with the same React tree the browser then hydrates.
portfolio.case.arch.locales.title: Five locales on clean routes
portfolio.case.arch.locales.body: English, Turkish, German, Spanish and French each have their own indexable addresses, with canonical and alternate links generated from the route registry.
portfolio.case.arch.runtimes.title: Separate game runtimes
portfolio.case.arch.runtimes.body: Each game is its own script or module, requested only on its page. Merge Rush's engine is requested only when Play is pressed.
portfolio.case.connected.title: The catalog can be read three ways.
portfolio.case.connected.body: Works shows the same catalog as a grid, as a System Map and as a Capability View. Every node and wire comes from the catalog's own categories; nothing on the map is drawn by hand. The relations listed under the catalog are only ones that are true of the code or the product.
portfolio.case.products.title: Four games, each with a way in and a way out.
portfolio.case.products.joyday: A canvas painting studio with palette moods and image export.
portfolio.case.products.flow: Wire a chatbot flow from nodes and ports across three authored levels.
portfolio.case.products.career: A deterministic drop-and-merge physics game with a career ladder.
portfolio.case.products.merge: A Phaser and TypeScript merge puzzle built in its own repository and shipped here as a build.
portfolio.case.ajoop.title: AJOOP answers from the published portfolio and shows its evidence.
portfolio.case.ajoop.body: The assistant retrieves from public portfolio data and falls back to deterministic answers when the model is unavailable. It keeps only a bounded copy of the current conversation in the tab's session storage. Owner-only tools sit behind a separate boundary and are not part of the public path. An owner cockpit is on the roadmap; it is not built.
portfolio.case.reliability.title: Every page has to work in the worst case first.
portfolio.case.reliability.nojs.title: Without JavaScript
portfolio.case.reliability.nojs.body: Content, navigation and links are in the HTML. The games and the assistant say what they need and offer another way on.
portfolio.case.reliability.motion.title: Motion, focus and keyboard
portfolio.case.reliability.motion.body: Reduced-motion preferences are honoured, focus is visible, and the interactive pieces can be operated from the keyboard.
portfolio.case.reliability.gates.title: Focused gates and review packs
portfolio.case.reliability.gates.body: Each phase ships with scripted checks on the production build and a captured review pack that is kept outside the repository.
portfolio.case.reliability.worktree.body: Work happens in an isolated worktree on a feature branch. The live checkout is never the development directory.
portfolio.case.privacy.title: Public by default, private by boundary.
portfolio.case.privacy.body: Private repositories are represented by their public product, never by a link. The catalog records a disposition for every repository, and a gate fails the build if a private address reaches a public page.
portfolio.case.status.title: What is in production, and what is still open.
portfolio.case.status.done: The five-language prerendered site, the connected Works catalog, AJOOP, four playable games and the complete coverage catalog.
portfolio.case.status.open: Real-device verification of the games, older source documents that still sit beside the generated pages, and the owner cockpit.
portfolio.case.cta.title: See the catalog this system renders.
aiFlow.case.v4.title: The same three levels, rebuilt as a mission-based game.
aiFlow.case.v4.ports.title: Wiring by ports
aiFlow.case.v4.ports.body: A connection starts at a node's output port and ends on another node. A trigger takes no input, and the ports themselves state the structural rules.
aiFlow.case.v4.diagnostics.title: Validation with diagnostics
aiFlow.case.v4.diagnostics.body: The verdict names what is wrong, including the nodes the trigger cannot reach, instead of a single pass or fail.
aiFlow.case.v4.scoring.title: Idempotent scoring
aiFlow.case.v4.scoring.body: Progress is stored per level and the score is the sum of the awards earned; validating or running a finished level again adds nothing.
aiFlow.case.v4.board.title: Pan, zoom and fit
aiFlow.case.v4.board.body: The board pans, zooms by wheel, pinch or buttons, and fits to the flow.
aiFlow.case.v4.missions.title: Missions and results
aiFlow.case.v4.missions.body: Choosing a mission enters a full-viewport mode with a briefing, the workspace and a result with a star rating.
aiFlow.case.v4.phone.title: Phone layout
aiFlow.case.v4.phone.body: On a tall board the flow is laid out top to bottom, with the ports on the top and bottom of each node.

joyday.case.paint.body: This portfolio hosts a small painting studio made for the same brand: choose a palette mood, throw paint at a canvas and export the result as an image. It is a separate, portfolio-native piece and not part of the business website.

request.v4.note: Every request is read by me, not routed through a queue. If the form does not confirm that your request was sent, email reaches me directly.
request.v4.direct.title: Prefer to talk first?
request.v4.direct.body: For roles, collaborations or a quick question, email or LinkedIn is the shortest path.
